name: Bluff Runner Windstrider
summary: On Thunder Bluff's mesas, Bluff Runner Windstrider carries urgent messages across the city. He directs Horde travelers toward distant frontiers, including Ashenvale, Feralas, and the Plaguelands.

sections.title: A Messenger on the Mesas
sections.body: Bluff Runner Windstrider carries messages across Thunder Bluff's high plateaus. His swift runs keep the city's leaders and visitors informed. He jogs along the rope bridges and pathways, calling out news and carrying dispatches. When outposts across Kalimdor or the Eastern Kingdoms need reinforcements, Windstrider calls on passing champions to carry word and answer the call to arms.

sections.title: Calls to the Frontier
sections.body: Bluff Runner Windstrider's messages reach far beyond Mulgore. He sends adventurers north to join Senani Thunderheart's great hunt at Splintertree Post in Ashenvale. He points seasoned scouts south toward Camp Mojache in Feralas and carries grave warnings about the ongoing undead menace in the Western Plaguelands. His dispatches connect Mulgore's tribal heart to the wider conflicts of the Horde.

faq.answer: Bluff Runner Windstrider carries messages across Thunder Bluff. He shares news and calls on capable Horde travelers to help with urgent campaigns across Azeroth.

faq.q: Where can I find Bluff Runner Windstrider?
faq.answer: Bluff Runner Windstrider jogs along Thunder Bluff's bridges and terraces. He often circles between the central mesa and neighboring rises.
Bluff Runner Windstrider directs travelers toward distant regions. His calls include the Ashenvale hunt, the establishment of Camp Mojache in Feralas, and calls to arms in the Plaguelands.

faq.q: Why is he called a 'Bluff Runner'?
faq.answer: Thunder Bluff's rugged mesas, cliffs, and suspended bridges can make mounted travel cumbersome or slow. Runners like Windstrider carry messages across the city on foot.

angles.text: As a member of the Horde, you can carry news from Mulgore to the fronts where the Horde fights for resources and survival.
As a tauren, you can follow the tradition of runners who keep the tribes and central elders connected without machinery or foreign post networks.
